judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale:
The element is the language switcher link in the header utility nav (Carta de Serviços, Concursos, English, Meu perfil), English. In the snapshot, html has lang="pt-br" and neither the link nor any ancestor carries a lang attribute, so the English word inherits pt-br, as the claim says (claimTrue yes). Under 3.1.2 the word does not fit an exception. It is the language's English name, not a proper name of a person, place or brand. It is not a technical term, its language is not indeterminate, and it is not vernacular Portuguese (Portuguese says 'Inglês'). A pt-BR voice reads it with Portuguese rules. The change of language is clearly intended: the text is the language's name in that language. Understanding 3.1.2 gives this exact case, 'Alternative language links', as an example: each link carries a lang attribute matching its language. The H58 test (the element's content must match its inherited language) fails here, so elementFails is yes, and the claim names that failure.
